slides.content: Carry = the return if market conditions stay constant; return = carry + E(price appreciation) + shock; futures C = (S-F)/F; directly observable ex ante; generalized UIP/EH test.

Clickable per-class definitions with formulas: FX interest differential; equities E(D)/S - rf with Gordon link; commodities convenience yield - rf; bonds slope - D x rolldown (YTM curve figure); options -theta + vega x vol-rolldown.

Yen-Aussie Nov 2007 (0.87% vs 7.09%); z = (i*-i) - ds; REAL cross-section: skewness declines in carry (AUD -0.32 ... JPY +0.32), risk reversals ditto (NZD -0.47 ... JPY +1.06), speculator positions rise in carry (JPY -0.097 ... CAD +0.059); up the stairs, down the elevator.
7.09-0.87=6.22; funding-currency appreciation of 2% cuts it to 4.22.

REAL panel regressions on i*-i by horizon: z(t+1) 2.17 fading to -0.04 at t+10; futures 8.26 fading; skewness -23.92 persisting to t+9 (-12.9): carry predicts returns (UIP violation), positioning, and CRASH RISK.

REAL: dVIX x sign(carry): futures -1.47, risk reversals -5.33, returns -0.43; after losses skewness rises (z coeff -3.34) but insurance price RISES (RiskRev on z +7.87 - the earthquake effect, slow-moving capital); co-movement |i1-i2| coefficient -10.89: carry creates a common factor.

Speculators partly correct UIP but their own funding constraints create endogenous crash risk that limits arbitrage - the forward premium puzzle survives; links to L6 BAB (funding) and L7 (tradability).

REAL Sharpe bars carry vs EW per 9 classes (equities 0.88 vs 0.32; puts 1.80 vs -1.01; commodities 0.60 vs 0.08) + Global Carry Factor: mean 6.75, vol 6.12, SR 1.10, skew -0.02, cumulative plot vs currency carry.
6.75/6.12=1.10; 1.80-(-1.01)=2.81. And note the skewness: -0.02 diversified vs -0.68 for currency carry alone.

REAL static-vs-dynamic decomposition (% dynamic: equities 101, slope 99, puts 100, Treasuries 42, credit 30): carry is a timing signal more than a tilt; cross-class carry correlations tiny (max 0.31) - diversification is the engine; carry distinct from value/momentum (GCF alpha 0.44-0.53, t>5.5, IR 1.05-1.24).

REAL: liquidity-shock exposures (currencies +0.88 t3.62, credit +1.24 t3.78), volatility exposures (currencies -1.03 t-6.46), expansions vs drawdowns per class, and the three GCF drawdowns 1972-75 -19.6% / 1980-82 -26.8% / 2008-09 -7.2% - all spanning recessions.
Expansion minus drawdown mean: 10.06-(-6.81)=16.87; 21.49-(-13.23)=34.72 - the state-dependence that a risk story needs.

Carry rejects UIP/EH in every class; expected returns vary over time and across assets and are observable ex ante; compensation looks like recession + liquidity + volatility risk, not simple crash risk at the global level; course links: L1 Gordon, L6 BAB, L7 robustness gauntlet applied.
